name: Gluttony

counsel.text: A gracious person holds the golden bridle of temperance; he takes his meat as a medicine to heal the decays of nature, that he may be the fitter, by the strength he receives, for the service of God; he makes his food, not fuel for lust, but help to duty.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, man's chief end

counsel.text: God allows recruits of nature, and what may fit us the better for his service; but beware of surfeit. Excess in the creature clouds the mind, chokes good affections, and provokes lust.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the seventh commandment

counsel.text: Consider what ways, what companies, what opportunities, what studies, what businesses, what conditions, have at any time given, or do usually give, advantages to thy distempers, and set thyself heedfully against them all. Men will do this with respect unto their bodily infirmities and distempers. The seasons, the diet, the air that have proved offensive shall be avoided. Are the things of the soul of less importance?
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

counsel.text: Set faith at work on Christ for the killing of thy sin. His blood is the great sovereign remedy for sin-sick souls. Live in this, and thou wilt die a conqueror; yea, thou wilt, through the good providence of God, live to see thy lust dead at thy feet.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: The forethoughts of affliction would make us sober and moderate in the use of lawful delight; it would cure a surfeit. Christ at a feast mentions his burial; a good antidote against a surfeit.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson

counsel.text: Those that would be content in the want of mercy, must be moderate in the enjoyment. Jonathan dipt the rod in honey, he did not thrust it in. Let us take heed of ingulphing ourselves in pleasure; better have a spare diet, than, by having too much, to surfeit.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 14

counsel.text: Consider how little will suffice nature. The body is but a small continent, and is easily recruited. Christ hath taught us to pray for our daily bread; nature is content with a little.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 14

counsel.text: That honey is sweet, it is not a conceit only, but the natural quality of it is so; yet out of a taste of the sweetness, to think we cannot take too much of it, is a misconceit paid home with loathsome bitterness.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 13

counsel.text: The body naturally desires food and bodily contentments, yet in a man endued with reason, this desire is governed so as it becomes not inordinate. A beast sins not in its appetite, because it hath no power above to order it.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 12

counsel.text: A full body makes a heavy eye and drowsy spirits; and what can then be expected but yawning prayers, especially when we are to continue longer than ordinary at the work?
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: O! how many are there in the world, whose backs are bravely clad with scarlet, while their souls embrace the dunghill—whose bellies are high fed and deliciously pampered, but their souls set at coarse fare!
counsel.author: William Gurnall

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Bountiful Father, every good thing I eat comes from your hand, and you give food in due season to all that live. I come through Jesus Christ. I confess that I have sinned in eating. I have eaten far beyond need, without thanks, and without thought of your glory. I have run to food for comfort, escape, and reward, as if it could fill the place in my heart that belongs to you. I have made my belly a god, and I have let appetite rule where your Spirit should rule. I do not want only to be free of what it does to my body; teach me to hate it because it has made a gift into an idol. Forgive me, Lord. Christ, hungry in the wilderness, would not turn stones into bread, but lived by every word that comes from your mouth. He is the bread of life, and whoever comes to him shall not hunger. For his sake pardon me. Holy Spirit, put this gluttony to death, and grow in me the fruit of self-control. Teach me to eat and drink to your glory, with thanks and with enough. I thank you that you satisfy the longing soul and fill the hungry soul with good things. In Jesus' name. Amen.

prayers.title: When I want more
prayers.text: Lord, I have had enough, and still I want more. Stop me here. Remind me that man does not live by bread alone. Whatever I am really hungry for right now, whether comfort, rest, or company, let me bring it to you instead. You are the bread of life. Help me put the food away, give thanks for what I have eaten, and turn to the next thing you have for me. Lord Jesus, you were hungry and did not give way. Holy Spirit, give me self-control. Amen.

prayers.title: For a thankful table
prayers.text: Father, teach me to receive food as your gift, with thanks, and to stop when I have had enough. Make my meals times of gratitude and fellowship rather than escape. Help me care for this body as your temple, neither despising it nor indulging it. If my eating has gone beyond my control, give me humility to seek help. Satisfy me with yourself, so that I do not look to food for what only you can give. Whether I eat or drink, or whatever I do, let me do it all to your glory. Through Jesus Christ. Amen.

prayers.title: That we may not make a god of our belly
prayers.text: We know that every thing is sanctified by the word of God and prayer; and that man lives not by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God; and therefore, according to our Master's example, we look up to heaven, and pray for a blessing upon our food, abundantly bless our provision. Lord, grant that we may not feed ourselves without fear, that we may not make a god of our belly, that our hearts may never be overcharged with surfeiting or drunkenness, but that whether we eat or drink, or whatever we do, we may do all to the glory of God.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry

examinationQuestions: When you reached for more today, what were you really hungry for: comfort, escape, relief from worry, or company?
Have you been treating food as a refuge, a place to run to that belongs to God alone?
What places, hours, or moods have most often led you into excess, and have you set yourself against them?
Are you receiving food with thanks, and eating so that you are more fit to serve God, not less?
Is there anyone you have hidden this from who should know, such as your pastor or a brother or sister in your church?
If eating feels out of your control, or you swing between eating too much and too little, have you told your pastor and seen a doctor?
fleeActions: Put the food away, close the cupboard, and leave the room.
Drink a glass of water, then step outside and walk for ten minutes, praying as you go.
Call or text a brother or sister in your church and tell them plainly that you are tempted right now.
Open your Bible to John 6 and read it slowly, out loud if you can.
Wait ten minutes before you eat anything more, and pray through Psalm 34 while you wait.
Give thanks out loud for what you have already eaten, and let that be the end of the meal.

afterFallReadings.text: Consider his mercifulness, tenderness, and kindness, as he is our great High Priest at the right hand of God. Assuredly he pities thee in thy distress; saith he, "As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you," Isa. 66:13. He hath the tenderness of a mother to a sucking child.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

afterFallReadings.text: The people of God have sins of daily occurrence; and, besides these, they sometimes lapse into great sins, and God is provoked, and his justice is ready to break forth upon them: but Christ's intercession is ready at hand, he daily makes up the breaches between God and them; he presents the merits of his blood to his Father, to pacify him.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: A Body of Divinity, Christ's priestly office
